title: Trance
description: Supersaw chords, gated pads, arpeggios, sidechain and the 32-bar build, at 138 BPM.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: Trance basics
tracks.blurb: A pad, a gate, an arp, the pump, the build, then an anthem.

lessons.title: Supersaw chords
lessons.goal: Make a wide, detuned trance chord that rings on.
lessons.concept:
Trance grew out of Frankfurt clubs and Goa beaches in the early 90s, and by the end of the decade its sound was the **supersaw**: seven sawtooth waves slightly out of tune with each other, so one chord sounds like a wall of strings.

`s("supersaw")` gives you that oscillator. `.unison(7)` sets how many voices, `.detune(.4)` how far apart they drift. A long `.release` lets each chord hang into the next, which is where the euphoria lives.

We play one chord per bar with `< >`, in A minor: the key half the genre is written in.

tasks.text: Add a part called pad: a supersaw playing one chord per bar from "<[a3,c4,e4] [f3,a3,c4] [c4,e4,g4] [g3,b3,d4]>".
tasks.hint: const pad = note("<[a3,c4,e4] [f3,a3,c4] [c4,e4,g4] [g3,b3,d4]>").s("supersaw").gain(.35), then stack(kick, clap, pad).

tasks.text: Let each chord ring into the next with a long release.

challenge.text: Take the fizz off the top with a low-pass around 1500 Hz.

summary: supersaw = several detuned saws at once.
.unison sets the voices, .detune how far apart.
A long .release makes chords ring into each other.

lessons.title: Gated pads
lessons.goal: Chop a held pad into pumping 16ths.
lessons.concept:
A trance pad rarely just sits there. Producers ran pads through a **gate** driven by the sequencer, so the chord stutters in 16ths and locks to the kick.

In Strudel the gate is `.struct`: it gives a pattern a new rhythm. `.struct("x*16")` retriggers the chord sixteen times a bar. `.clip(.5)` makes each hit last half its step, which is the gap that makes it pump.

Change the pattern of x and ~ and you have a different gate rhythm: the trance trick of the late 90s.

tasks.text: Gate the pad: retrigger the chord on every 16th.
Shorten each hit to half a step so the gate breathes.

challenge.text: Give the gate a rhythm: play three 16ths, rest one, four times a bar.

summary: .struct("x*16") retriggers a chord in 16ths: a gate.
.clip shortens each hit so the gate pumps.
Rests in the struct pattern make a gate rhythm.

lessons.title: The arpeggio
lessons.goal: Run a 16th-note arpeggio over the chords.
lessons.concept:
The arpeggio is trance’s melody machine: the chord’s notes played one at a time, fast, up and down. On hardware it was an **arpeggiator**; here it is `.arp`.

`.arp("[0 1 2 1]*4")` plays note 0, 1, 2, 1 of each chord (0 is the lowest), four times a bar: sixteen notes that follow the chord as it changes.

A sawtooth through a low-pass with a little resonance keeps it bright but not harsh, and a slow filter sweep makes it come alive.

tasks.text: Add a part called arp: the same chords, arpeggiated 0 1 2 1 in 16ths on a sawtooth.
tasks.hint: const arp = note("<[a3,c4,e4] [f3,a3,c4] [c4,e4,g4] [g3,b3,d4]>").arp("[0 1 2 1]*4").s("sawtooth").gain(.4), then stack(kick, clap, pad, arp).

tasks.text: Filter it: cutoff 1200 Hz with a touch of resonance.

challenge.text: Sweep the arp’s filter on an 8-bar sine between 600 and 2400 Hz.

summary: .arp("0 1 2 1") plays a chord one note at a time.
A filtered sawtooth is the classic arp voice.
A slow sine on the cutoff keeps it moving.

lessons.title: Sidechained pads
lessons.goal: Make the kick pump the pad.
lessons.concept:
The trance pump: every kick pushes the pad down, and the pad swells back up between kicks. In a studio that is a compressor **sidechained** to the kick; in Strudel it is **ducking**.

Ducking works per **orbit**. Put the pad on its own orbit, then tell the kick to duck that orbit: `.duckorbit(2)` names it, `.duckdepth(.8)` says how far down, `.duckattack(.3)` how quickly it comes back.

It only works on an orbit something is playing on, so the pad goes on orbit 2 first.

tasks.text: Put the pad on its own orbit, number 2.
Duck orbit 2 from the kick, 80% deep.

challenge.text: Slow the recovery so the swell is audible.

summary: Ducking is per orbit: the pad gets its own.
.duckorbit(n).duckdepth(d) on the kick pumps that orbit.
.duckattack sets how fast the pad swells back.

lessons.title: The 32-bar build and the drop
lessons.goal: Raise the tension for 32 bars, then let everything in.
lessons.concept:
Trance is built in 32-bar blocks. The **build** takes away the kick, adds a **riser** (noise whose high-pass climbs for 32 bars) and opens the pad’s filter slowly, so the room leans forward. Then the **drop**: kick, bass, everything.

Two long signals do the work: `saw.range(200, 8000).slow(32)` on the riser’s `.hpf`, and `saw.range(300, 4000).slow(32)` on the pad’s `.lpf`. Both climb for 32 bars and reset.

A snare roll in the last bar, `.mask("<0!31 1>")`, is the classic cue that the drop is coming.

tasks.text: Add a part called riser: pink noise whose high-pass climbs from 200 to 8000 Hz over 32 bars.
tasks.hint: const riser = s("pink*16").hpf(saw.range(200, 8000).slow(32)).gain(.2), then stack it.

tasks.text: Open the pad’s filter over the same 32 bars, from 300 to 4000 Hz.

challenge.text: Add a snare roll in bar 32 only: 16 snares, masked out of the other 31 bars.

summary: A build: riser up, filter opening, over 32 bars.
saw.range(a, b).slow(32) climbs for 32 bars and resets.

lessons.title: Project: A trance anthem
lessons.goal: Arrange the pad, arp and riser into intro, build and drop.
lessons.concept:
Everything from this pack in the shape of a record: a drum **intro** a DJ can mix, a 32-bar **build** with the riser and the pad opening but no kick, and the **drop** with the kick ducking the pad and the arp on top.

One `const key` keeps the arp in tune, so moving the whole anthem to another key is one edit. Sections are named stacks; `arrange()` plays them in turn, and each section restarts its own clock, so the 32-bar sweeps line up with the build.

tasks.text: Put the key in one place: const key = "A3:minor", and make the arp use it.
tasks.hint: const key = "A3:minor" near the top, then .scale(key) on the arp.

tasks.text: Name three sections: intro (kick, hats), build (hats, clap, pad, arp, riser) and drop (everything but the riser). Keep playing drop for now.
tasks.hint: const intro = stack(kick, hats), const build = stack(hats, clap, pad, arp, riser), const drop = stack(kick, clap, hats, pad, arp); end with drop.

tasks.text: Arrange them: 16 bars of intro, 32 of build, 32 of drop.
tasks.hint: Replace the last line with arrange([16, intro], [32, build], [32, drop]).

challenge.text: Add a 16-bar drum outro after the drop.
challenge.hint: const outro = stack(kick, hats), then arrange([16, intro], [32, build], [32, drop], [16, outro]).

summary: Intro, 32-bar build, drop: the trance shape.
One const key keeps the melody parts in tune.
Sections are named stacks; arrange() plays them in turn.
